items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1971-04-20
items.q: We had, uh, we think from the piano. We had Lil Hardin on piano. We had Johnny Dotson on Clionet. Joe Oliver on trumpet. Nora Dutre on trombone. Uh, we had, uh, Jimmy Polar on violin. Uh, we had a band. And I was on the bass.

ctx.x: They fired Jimmy Polar. Oh yeah. I remember that. You see, I'll give you the lineup of the band we left fairly well with. We had, uh, we think from the piano. We had Lil Hardin on piano. We had Johnny Dotson on Clionet. Joe Oliver on trumpet. Nora Dutre on trombone. Uh, we had, uh, Jimmy Polar on violin. Uh, we had a band. And I was on the bass. Ram was on the drums. Okay. Then, they want to turn this boy loose, give him a note. Didn't give him no notice. Just fired him.

items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1957-04-16
items.q: We went there with King Oliver's Nine Kings... myself on bass, and King Oliver was playing.

ctx.x: No, no, no, no, no. There wasn't no big girls there, no. Dancing? Dancing and entertaining. Billy Bottoms had the same thing across the way. Then Billy Bottoms, they all got crazy about the jazz band. I could get a job all around. The first time I went to the union, all right, here come the walking delegate now. The walking delegate come up, talking about, I have to join the union. I said, you crazy. I ain't stood about no union. You ain't going to mess me up. You all need to join the union so you can take me off…
Yes. I'm trying to. Pull that loose. I'm not tearing it. You see, Copeland was second time.

items.title: 68090_Ed Garland oral history interview
items.q: "That was King Oliver's group, I was working see?"

ctx.x: When I left there, we come on down to Los Angeles, to play with Jelly Roll of a Friday and -- of a Saturday and Sunday. At Leek's Lake (Unintelligible). He used to run dances there. We played down there with them. That was King Oliver's group, I was working see?

items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1957-04-16
items.q: I was playing with they used to play with him in New Orleans you see he played with us with Oliver but when after I got up there Wages Williams wanted to open up the up the the this the Royal Garden and I sent for Joe for him off to play for him yeah I see then after Joe come up then we got together

ctx.x: Oh yeah? Garland's New Orleans Jazz Band. Uh-huh. Jazz band, yeah.

Then, uh, Johnny Dodds come in town. We got a hold of Johnny Dodds. Nora Dutre was in the neighborhood. He used to come into Chicago and he'd come sit in with us. So, uh, Boyd H. Williams opened up the, uh, the, opened up this club on 34th Street, uh, Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland…
Was it hard to find a piano player at the time?
